validation_question: What lanes are required before threshold changes?
current_answer: At least one CI lane plus one comparable local or container lane; browser alternatives are causal checks, not threshold lanes.
required_lanes: Exact Playwright-bundled Chromium on CI, local host Chromium when available, same wp-env/container shape used by CI, and optional Firefox/WebKit timer-timeline lanes.
minimum_rows: Compact discriminating row set only; do not start with the full dense sweep.
required_metadata: CPU model, core count, OS version, browser revision, Playwright version, wp-env/container limits, power mode, thermal pressure if available, process QoS, background load, and git/build identifiers.
expansion_trigger: Expand to the full dense sweep only if a compact row changes qualitative band, variance class, timer ordering, or visual endpoint direction.
allowed_claim: May change absolute thresholds only after CI Chromium and at least one comparable lane preserve qualitative ordering and bound p50/CV movement.

validation_question: Which score rows are the compact minimum?
current_answer: Rows should exercise mechanisms, not cover every delay.
required_lanes: All threshold lanes; optional causal lanes use the subset with comparable metrics.
minimum_rows: CI current held key, tap/complete-keypress baseline, 990/1000/1010/1300 held-key boundary, 50ms and 100ms hold controls, pattern 500ms and 1000ms readiness rows, runtime checkpoint controls, CPU/QoS controls, and visual endpoint controls.
required_metadata: For each score row, keep retained samples, throwaway count, per-run p50, p10/p90, CV, first-three-key distribution, sample order, and elapsed suite time.
expansion_trigger: Missing retained-sample policy, first-key behavior, or sample-order data invalidates threshold interpretation.
allowed_claim: Can claim qualitative portability only when row ordering and regime labels match across lanes; cannot claim threshold portability from ordering alone.

validation_question: How should startup/setup confounds be handled?
current_answer: Local randomized/exact and fresh-editor checks bound setup locally but not on CI.
required_lanes: Repeat exact-spec randomized blocks on CI with fresh saved/reopened drafts and the current no-extra-wait Typing setup.
minimum_rows: 0ms, 1000ms, and 60000ms start-wait controls where feasible; otherwise a smaller exact-spec 0ms versus current-CI setup pair.
required_metadata: setupReady time, runStart time, first key timing, first-three-key distribution, retained/throwaway policy, resource counts moved before first key, and suite elapsed time.
expansion_trigger: If first-input behavior or retained run-p50 medians diverge outside local volatility, add CI-specific startup/setup diagnostics before changing thresholds.
allowed_claim: May keep local measurement semantics if ordering holds; may not reuse local absolute p50 as a CI threshold.

validation_question: How should browser coverage be interpreted?
current_answer: Only Playwright-bundled Chromium should set Chrome thresholds; Firefox/WebKit are causal portability checks.
required_lanes: Run Chrome threshold lane first; run Firefox/WebKit timer-timeline diagnostics only to verify timer ordering and broad mechanism direction.
minimum_rows: 990/1000/1010 timer timeline, listener/input spans where supported, and visual endpoint checks when available.
required_metadata: Browser engine, revision, trace categories, metric definitions, and whether spans are comparable to Chromium EventDispatch.
expansion_trigger: If Firefox/WebKit preserve timer ordering but not magnitudes, do not use their p50 values for Chromium thresholds; if timer ordering changes, reopen the causal story.
allowed_claim: May cite causal portability across engines, not threshold equivalence.

validation_question: How should container and wp-env portability be separated?
current_answer: The existing Columns fixture is not a host-versus-container isolation experiment.
required_lanes: Run the same compact row set inside the CI-like wp-env/container and on a comparable local host shape when possible.
minimum_rows: Same post fixture and same input helper across host/container lanes; include a separate fixture-size control only after host/container comparison.
required_metadata: Docker resource limits, CPU/memory limits, storage backend, network mode, browser sandbox flags, wp-env config, and fixture hash.
expansion_trigger: If host/container ordering differs, split threshold and product claims by environment before adding new benchmark rows.
allowed_claim: May set environment-specific thresholds only for environments with measured validation lanes.

validation_question: How should power and scheduler state affect validation?
current_answer: It is threshold-critical metadata because CPU/QoS controls can move the same path between slow and fast bands.
required_lanes: Pair the compact row set with lightweight power/QoS metadata; pair suspicious rows with the CPU/QoS counter runset.
minimum_rows: At minimum include one no-CPU slow row, one ordinary/utility fast row, one background/maintenance slow row, and one finite-burst decay row when investigating system drift.
required_metadata: Power mode, thermal pressure if available, process QoS, background CPU load, core/frequency/residency counters when available, and browser scheduler markers for suspicious rows.
expansion_trigger: If p50 movement correlates with power/QoS state, thresholds must be stratified or rerun under controlled state; do not average states together.
allowed_claim: May explain drift as environment state only when metadata is present per sample or per run.

validation_question: What can change before the runbook is executed?
current_answer: Measurement semantics and low-risk source patches can proceed; absolute thresholds cannot.
required_lanes: Local source patches with behavior tests, artifact-scoping documentation, and compact diagnostic rows that do not assert new absolute thresholds.
minimum_rows: No threshold-moving rows required before these local decisions, but record which local evidence each decision uses.
required_metadata: Patch identity, behavior-test result, benchmark helper semantics, and whether a claim is artifact, source, product, or threshold scoped.
expansion_trigger: If a change needs a numeric CI acceptance band, this runbook must run first.
allowed_claim: May claim local causal or source-path evidence; may not claim portable p50/CV or move CI thresholds.
